names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 martie, «Sfântul Mucenic Conon din Isauria».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Κόνων ο Ίσαυρος», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 5 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Конон Исавријски.“, with the rank word мученик left off and Свети, which is not a rank. Исавријски is kept: it is the epithet of his country and it is what the Prologue uses to tell him from the Conon of the next entry.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 5 марта ст. ст., name page 1266, «Конон Исаврийский, исповедник», with the rank and grade words left off. The day's own line declines the name. The rank word left off here is исповедник, confessor, which is not the grade the line itself gives him; that difference is on the attestation row and in the life. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 марта ст. ст. — «Мч. Конона Исаврийского (I)»

attestations.note: **The line and its own name link grade him differently.** The line says Мч., martyr, and the link behind it heads him «Конон Исаврийский, исповедник», confessor — and the life behind the line has him rescued from the torturers by his own townsmen and dying in peace two years afterwards. Nothing is added to `types` on that account and nothing taken away: the grade is the author's to settle, and the reading is set out in the life. The line's century, (I), is also not the century this folder records for his death.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Conon din Isauria»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Κόνων ο Ίσαυρος»

attestations.note: The page puts his birth «περί τα τέλη του 1ου αιώνα μ.Χ. στη Βαδινή, χωριό της Ισαυρίας της Μικράς Ασίας» and says he lived in the apostolic times. It names his parents Nestor and Nada, both idolaters at first, and says his father Nestor was martyred for Christ; the day's own list keeps that Nestor as an entry of his own. It reports from the synaxarion that the Archangel Michael himself guided him, baptised him, taught him the Name of the Holy Trinity, gave him the divine Mysteries to the end of his life and granted him the grace of strange wonders. It names the archon Magnus who arrested and tortured him after the idols of a temple broke in pieces at his prayer, and says he reposed in peace two years after being released. It adds, with its own «Ίσως», perhaps, that a church in his name may have stood beyond Constantinople and is mentioned as a monastery under Justinian I (527–565); that hedge is the site's and is not acted on. It says that in the years of the iconoclasm Christians carried his holy skull to Paphos, where it is kept to this day at the monastery of Chrysorrogiatissa in an elegant mother-of-pearl case.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.03.2026 (5. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Конон Исавријски.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, and the heading carries the epithet that keeps him apart from the day's second Conon, so the stored Serbian form keeps it too. The folder held a birth and no death; the Prologue states the century of his life and his suffering and the death was added from it. The two statements of century are not quite the same: saint.gr puts his birth about the end of the first century and has him live «στους Αποστολικούς χρόνους», in the apostolic times, where the Prologue puts both his life and his suffering in the second. The birth interval was left exactly as it was and the tension is recorded in the death's note.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Conon, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Conon din Isauria

english.text: Thy martyr Conon, O Lord, in his contest received the crown of incorruption from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength he overcame his tormentors, and broke the strengthless daring of the demons. At his prayers, O Christ our God, save Thou our souls.

hymns.text: Τὴν χάριν τοῦ Πνεύματος, ἐνδεδυμένος σοφέ, τὸ κράτος διέλυσας, τῆς ἀσεβείας στερρῶς. Ἐκλάμπων τοὶς θαύμασιν ὅθεν πεφοινιγμένος, ταὶς ροαὶς τῶν αἱμάτων. Κόνων Ὁσιομάρτυς, τὸν Δεσπότην δοξάζεις, τὸν παρέχοντα ἠμὶν διὰ σοῦ, χάριν καὶ ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, on the page of Άγιος Κόνων ο Ίσαυρος. It names him and calls him Ὁσιομάρτυς, venerable martyr, which is the rank the page's hymns give him although its life has him die in peace. The page also prints a megalynarion and a kathisma, for which the corpus's schema has no kind; the apolytikion and the kontakion are the two taken here.

english.text: Clothed in the grace of the Spirit, O wise one, thou didst break up steadfastly the dominion of impiety, shining out with wonders; whence, made crimson with the flowing of thy blood, O Conon, venerable martyr, thou glorifiest the Master, who through thee bestoweth grace and mercy upon us.

hymns.text: Ἀγγελικῆς ἀξιωθείς ὀπτασίας, τήν ἐν Χριστῷ μεμυσταγώγησαι πίστιν, καί τῶν θαυμάτων εἴληφας τήν δύναμιν σοφέ· ὅθεν καθυπέταξας, τήν ὀφρύν τῶν δαιμόνων, καί τῆς πλάνης ἔσβεσας, ἐναθλήσας τήν φλόγα. Ὁσιομάρτυς Κόνων Ἀθλητά, ἐξευμενίζου ἡμῖν τόν Φιλάνθρωπον.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ὁ ὑψωθείς, on the page of Άγιος Κόνων ο Ίσαυρος. It names him and names the angelic vision his life turns on, and the subduing of the demons.

english.text: Counted worthy of an angelic vision, thou wast initiated into the faith in Christ and didst receive the power of wonders, O wise one; whence thou didst bring low the arrogance of the demons and, contending, didst quench the flame of error. O Conon, venerable martyr and contender, make the Lover of mankind merciful towards us.

hymns.text: Яко девственника предивна/ и мученика непоколебима,/ блаженнаго страдальца,/ на бесы власть приемшаго,/ Конона песньми восхвалим и к нему возопиим:/ моли Христа Бога,/ да спасет души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 марта ст. ст. — «Тропарь мученика Конона Исаврийского»

english.text: As a virgin most wondrous and a martyr unshaken, the blessed sufferer who received power over the demons, let us praise Conon with hymns and cry out unto him: pray thou to Christ God, that he may save our souls.

hymns.text: Чистотою яко Ангел на земли пожив,/ отонудуже собеседник Ангелом быти сподобился еси,/ и родители ко Христову познанию привел еси,/ и, единаго Бога в Троице исповедав,/ пострадал еси до крове,/ мучениче Кононе,/ моли Его непрестанно о всех нас.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 марта ст. ст. — «Кондак мученика Конона Исаврийского»

english.text: Having lived on earth in purity like an angel, thou wast therefore accounted worthy to be a companion of angels; and thou didst bring thy parents to the knowledge of Christ, and, having confessed one God in Trinity, thou didst suffer even unto blood. O martyr Conon, pray unto him unceasingly for us all.

birth.display: about the end of the 1st century
birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Κόνων γεννήθηκε περί τα τέλη του 1ου αιώνα μ.Χ. στη Βαδινή, χωριό της Ισαυρίας της Μικράς Ασίας και έζησε στους Αποστολικούς χρόνους» — the page's «περί τα τέλη», about the end, is why the bounds are a quarter-century and not a year. doxologia.ro, from which this folder was first written, gives him no year at all, and saint.gr gives none for his repose.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 5 March: „Овај дивни светитељ поживе и пострада у II веку.“ It gives the century and no year, and the folder carried no death at all before this reading. The saint.gr sentence quoted on the birth above sets him in the apostolic times, which reads as the first century rather than the second; the interval here is the Prologue's own and the disagreement is not resolved.
